To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proposed self-supervised training pipeline for event-based optical-flow estimation can train ANNs and SNSs with similar accuracy, and that SNNs trained with this pipeline can learn to predict optical flow with a high degree of accuracy, even with sparse and asynchronous inputs.

(1) the proposed pipeline enables learning optical flow with event-based cameras with ANNs and SPPS SNNs; (2) SNNs can learn optical flow from event inputs; and (3) adaptive SNNs can outperform nonadaptive SNNs in the proposed pipeline.
the proposed training pipeline enables SNNs to learn to estimate event-based optical flow in a self-supervision setting.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (i) How can we modify the state-ofthe- art ANN training pipeline to make it more suitable for neuromorphic hardware and enable learning of complex tasks with event-based inputs? (ii) How does learning with event-based optical flow in SNNs differ from learning with the same data in ANN?

developing the necessary tools and understanding to enable the application of SNNs to real-time, large-scale, complex, and low-power regression tasks, such as the estimation of optical flow from event cameras.
developing a new training pipeline for SNNs that is capable of learning to estimate complex spatio-temporal information from event-based cameras.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed training pipeline is effective in training both ANNs and SNSs for event-based optical-flow estimation.
the proposed pipeline and the SNNs trained with it can achieve competitive optical flow estimation performance with event-based inputs.

the proposed SNN training pipeline is capable of learning to solve a complex, high-resolution, and high-dimensional regression problem from event-based camera data, and that the performance of such networks is on par with that achieved with ANNs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed self-supervised training pipeline can be successfully used with both ANN and SNN architectures.
the proposed pipeline and loss function are a promising starting point for learning event-based optical flow with SNNs.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of learning to perform optical flow estimation with SNNs in a fully neuromorphic manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that

SNNs can be trained to perform complex regression tasks with minimal temporal information encoded in their inputs, and that the performance gap to ANNs can be closed by using the proposed self-supervised learning pipeline.
SNNs can indeed learn complex regression tasks with event-based inputs in a fully asynchronous manner.
, with the right training pipeline and loss function, it is possible to train SNNs with sparse inputs, and that the performance of such SNNs can be comparable to that of ANNs.
